comments: Every empirical claim in the PRD was verified in-pod on kbhub (hostname jupyter-chenry) on 2026-07-31/2026-08-01 against the live platform and installed packages.

HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING: the guides' 'auto-imported, no imports needed' claim holds only inside a notebook kernel. A skill in a terminal gets ImportError. The verified import map in the PRD is the single most important thing the skills encode.
DOC ERROR 1: data_lakehouse_ingest docstrings claim it writes Silver Delta tables. It writes Iceberg via writeTo; there is no Delta write path in the package.
DOC ERROR 2: the installed package exposes namespace ACLs, stewardship, tenancy v2, cluster management, and an MCP client family that appear in none of the ten guides.
KBUTILLIB GAP: KBBERDLUtils does not read KBASE_AUTH_TOKEN and raises 'No KBase token available' even in-pod where that variable is set and works. Token precedence must be env -> file -> config.
SAFETY: the credential escalation ladder must try the non-rotating fix first. refresh_spark_environment() rotates credentials and breaks other live kernels, scripts, and remote connections.
SAFETY: AccessDenied on cross-tenant prefixes is expected isolation, not breakage. Misreading it leads directly to the damaging rotating fix.
TRAP CONFIRMED RELEVANT: 'aws s3 ls .../kbase' also matches 'kbaseincubator' because prefix matching has no implicit trailing slash. This affects both initial target tenants.
Both target tenants are read-write for chenry, so no Slack access request is needed to begin.
Off-pod is not yet proven end to end: the REST route authenticates and needs no SSH tunnel, but token resolution off-pod is unfixed and the personal catalog did not appear in REST results.
Skill registration must be run from primary-laptop; a Linux register writes a non-portable home path and breaks macOS sync.
context: PRD rendered but NOT yet confronted, decomposed, or registered. Next steps: optional cross-family confront, then taskplan.json synthesis, validation via load_taskplan, and registration.
